searchText: _resumes lurking_ where can I get a chart with historical base_fee prices since 1559? Can't you query your own node? I'm not sure what the fastest way of doing it is, but eth_getBlockByNumber should work Because I got curious myself: Python script https://gist.github.com/pietjepuk2/5ac6a9954d57ce8ffb1e509c0b43909f CSV export: https://gist.githubusercontent.com/pietjepuk2/29df0310cc5a45e807ef5ddf58ecc5c8/raw/9090137bc6acd30fb389868fb361352ed8ea0a71/base_fee.csv yeah, but I was hoping to just click on a link here and see this, I'm sure this has to be out there ahh thanks, the python script is just as good 🙂 Is spinning up another chain a way to scale Ethereum? it depends on what you mean by that, you might want to read this article https://vitalik.ca/general/2021/05/23/scaling.html Imeant just taking the current state and deploying a completely separate chain. So execution could happen in this other chain (discretely) but we could bridge assets between them. economically speaking that would duplicate all of the assets on both ledgers, like the bcash fork off bitcoin but more
